summary: The estimator developed from analytic moments to learned corrections, a rebuilt signed-pair state, cheaper propagation and richer learned readouts. The two final variants share that development and differ in their last coefficient update.
limit: This path follows documented development milestones. Some intermediate versions are summarized; a connection is not automatically an immediate source-file parent. The independent core rebuild is identified explicitly. The final coefficient exports and runtime assembly are verified by hashes.

nodes.title: Feed the learned correction into every layer
nodes.claim: The earlier estimator corrected its output after propagation. The new model reads the current moment state at each layer, corrects the mean and covariance, and passes that corrected state forward. Honest training rows and a smaller fourth-order carrier produced #329754.

nodes.title: Rebuild the state around paired cubic columns
nodes.claim: An independently rebuilt moment model replaced the large fourth-order tensor with a covariance-shaped approximation. Two signed columns represented each new cubic contribution. The learned correction was retrained for this state; the resulting family reached #329926 after runtime repairs.

nodes.title: Fit the directions of newly created cubic terms
nodes.claim: Four fitted directions changed the cubic columns created after each ReLU while keeping the mean-correction heads fixed. The complete estimator improved on held networks and became #330390.

nodes.title: Combine learned birth and mean corrections
nodes.claim: The next candidate combined the learned birth correction with the existing mean encoder. The two saved models were composed without another fit, then the combined estimator was measured on held networks before subsequent carrier work.

nodes.title: Compress older cubic columns into one shared basis
nodes.claim: Recent cubic columns stayed explicit. Older cohorts were projected into one rank-384 basis and read together, reducing their computation. The constructor retained the learned mean and birth models already present in its parent.

nodes.title: The first compressed version timed out
nodes.claim: The rank-384 estimator looked viable in local timing, but #330840 timed out on every attempted hosted network. The representation was retained; the implementation needed fewer remote operations.

nodes.title: Make the compressed estimator run within the time limit
nodes.claim: Batched products, separate frame caches and a size-based multiplication schedule reduced remote calls. After two failed hosted versions, #330931 ran successfully with the same moment model and learned payload.

nodes.title: Restore full covariance and third-moment reads
nodes.claim: The estimator restored the full covariance, the repeated third-moment residual and the trace vector. Cubic masks, birth rules, rank-384 compression and learned parameters were held fixed, isolating the value of those lower-moment reads.

nodes.title: Learn a correction to late-layer covariance
nodes.claim: A learned pair model corrected covariance at layers 8–14 on the full-moment trajectory. Its measured gain survived packaging and hosted evaluation. This created a different trajectory for the mean model to learn from.

nodes.title: Refit the mean model on the corrected trajectory
nodes.claim: The mean encoder’s 45,200 parameters were refitted with the new covariance correction active. Birth parameters, covariance-edge weights and normalization stayed fixed. The refitted estimator became #331760.

nodes.title: Join older factors at layers 7, 10 and 13
nodes.claim: Older cubic factors were joined every third layer. The same candidate added a per-row fourth-cumulant correction and a trace-gain correction. This combination became #331947 and retained the mean and covariance models.

nodes.title: Fit the closure and recurrent encoder together
nodes.claim: Joint fitting updated the closure parameters and the recurrent encoder on the current estimator. The arithmetic structure was unchanged for this refit, so its improvement came from the learned coefficients rather than a different runtime route.

nodes.title: Build the shared basis with a Nyström sketch
nodes.claim: A Nyström sketch replaced the older join construction using selected Gram-matrix rows. The candidate also removed a residual-plane cross term and refitted its coefficients. This retained the compressed cubic state while making its updates cheaper.

nodes.title: Retain local fourth-order effects on young column pairs
nodes.claim: Two new terms used the existing young signed pairs: a fourth-order column shift fed information into later births, and a local kurtosis correction improved each neuron’s fourth moment. They were added without refitting the learned model in #333435.

nodes.title: Carry norm-coupling coefficients on the same pairs
nodes.claim: A derived norm-coupling correction was represented by one extra weight per column and one cross-weight per pair. It reused the cubic read instead of transporting a large extra matrix, preserving most of the useful correction at much lower cost.

nodes.title: Let the mean model read the new fourth-order signal
nodes.claim: After adding the young-pair quartic plane, one per-neuron norm-coupling statistic was supplied to the learned mean correction. Two fitted steps updated its new input weights while retaining the previously fitted physical coefficients.

nodes.title: Correct cubic transport for skewness and kurtosis
nodes.claim: The cubic transport gate gained skewness and kurtosis corrections. After further fitting of the same estimator, this mathematical change was combined with exact transform caching and validated as #335633.

nodes.title: Carry fourth-order corrections for older pairs
nodes.claim: The local fourth-moment correction was extended to pairs three and four layers old, first at the output and then through layers 8–14. The resulting #335782 retained those older contributions alongside further fitted coefficients and runtime reductions.

nodes.title: Keep corrected means nonnegative
nodes.claim: At layers 1–14, limit the learned change to max(delta, -mean) before updating both the mean and covariance. This keeps the updates consistent when the proposed mean would be negative. The submitted file also reuses covariance products to reduce arithmetic cost.

nodes.title: Use two directions for message and energy products
nodes.claim: Approximate the squared-weight message product and three energy products with rank-two output projections, retaining their constant component exactly. Added to #336075 with a request repair, this change passes accuracy and runtime checks and remains in later versions.

nodes.title: Approximate omitted young-factor reads with two directions
nodes.claim: Use a two-direction completion for the omitted part of the recent third-moment factor read. The tested approximation slightly worsens raw error but saves enough arithmetic to improve the adjusted score. A request-count repair makes this version deployable.

nodes.title: Build the shared basis from the strongest factor columns
nodes.claim: Refine the old-cohort Nystrom basis using heavily weighted columns and a symmetric core. Later tests settle on 1,536 / 1,024 / 1,024 sketch columns at joins 7 / 10 / 13. All joined columns still contribute to the factor projection; the sketch only constructs the basis.

nodes.title: Balance late-layer accuracy against read cost
nodes.claim: Restrict the final third-moment read to rows near the ReLU threshold, then retain more young-factor information in layers 13–14 and old-factor information in layer 14. These are measured approximation choices: each is checked with its own accuracy loss or gain and compute cost.

nodes.title: Reduce learned messages to eight channels
nodes.claim: Distill the learned message representation into eight channels while preserving the larger recurrent state. The submitted version also restores the loader operations needed for reliable execution. This smaller message model becomes the parent of the next readout improvements.

nodes.title: Compress the covariance model and refit the mean readout
nodes.claim: Reduce the covariance-correction model to eight hidden channels and fit a per-layer mean readout on 90 training networks. The combined model is tested on its own trajectory and becomes #337466, the baseline for the final hidden-feature readout experiments.

nodes.title: A second fit on the older readout fails the full estimator
nodes.claim: A parallel full-hidden readout branch improves cross-validation by 0.590%, but its actual adjusted score is 0.102% worse than #337506. Its gain against its own parent does not pay for the runtime-related arithmetic. This branch closes; it is distinct from the final 961-feature fit.

nodes.title: Use the encoder’s first hidden layer in the readout
nodes.claim: Add the encoder’s first 128 hidden activations to its learned output correction. Combine this with paid runtime repairs and remove an unused object-count diagnostic. Submission #337506 becomes the common source for both final coefficient exports.

nodes.title: Fit the output correction
nodes.claim: Run the parent on 90 training networks and fit an update to its output coefficients. The fit uses 961 features, ridge 0.03 and damping 0.5. Both releases use this same fit.

nodes.title: Update coefficients ×1.5
nodes.claim: Add the fitted update to the output coefficients at strength 1.5. The encoder and other learned tensors are unchanged by this export.

nodes.title: Set the runtime configuration
nodes.claim: Append the recorded runtime settings: grouped-read cap four, matrix-size threshold 8e9, and direct gather. The build manifest records exact input and output hashes.

nodes.title: Released estimator #337619
nodes.claim: Package the assembled source. The archived public score is 1.4005566073702658e-9, with zero failed networks. Both sources were designated for private re-evaluation.

nodes.title: Update coefficients ×1.35
nodes.claim: Add the fitted update to the output coefficients at strength 1.35. The encoder and other learned tensors are unchanged by this export.

nodes.title: Set the runtime configuration
nodes.claim: Append the recorded runtime settings: grouped-read cap four, matrix-size threshold 8e9, and direct gather. The build manifest records exact input and output hashes.

nodes.title: Released estimator #337641
nodes.claim: Remove the three inactive residual-meter function bodies, then package the source. The archived public score is 1.4006490071107744e-9, with zero failed networks. Both sources were designated for private re-evaluation.
